Overview

Franchising is IP licensing at scale: the brand, operating manual and know-how are licensed to franchisees, and the structure decides who owns what the franchisees build.

Registrations that are not renewed, recorded or used can weaken the very rights a business plans to enforce or license. Cross-border licences and technology transfers carry FEMA and withholding-tax consequences on the payments. Interim injunctions are often the decisive stage of an IP dispute, and courts look closely at delay, so acting quickly matters.

Enforcement cases are won on evidence gathered before the first letter — test purchases, screenshots, invoices — so we collect it first.

Who this applies to

  • A business with a large, unmanaged IP portfolio
  • A company licensing its technology or brand
  • A franchisor expanding through franchisees

Documents required

  • Evidence of infringement — samples, screenshots, invoices
  • Details of the counterparty, where known
  • Evidence of use and reputation
  • Existing licences, assignments and agreements
  • Registration certificates and pending applications

How the work proceeds

  1. 1

    Facts and objective

    We take the facts and what you are trying to achieve before forming a view.

  2. 2

    Written advice

    Our view is set out in writing, with the steps to implement it.

  3. 3

    Implementation support

    Filings, documents or representations that follow from the advice are handled as needed.

Customs IP Recordal (Anti-Counterfeiting)

Customs recordal lets a rights holder register its trademarks, copyright, designs or GIs with Indian Customs so that suspected counterfeit imports can be held at the border.
